key_insight: UNIEGO learns a richer egocentric video representation by using multiple proxy teachers to transfer complementary knowledge from other views, modalities, and foundation models into a single egocentric model. This lets the system stay deployable from first-person video alone while benefiting from broader supervision.
problem_solved: Egocentric video is inherently incomplete: a wearable camera sees only one viewpoint, one modality, and often misses context needed for robust action understanding. The paper addresses how to build a unified representation that captures more semantic richness without requiring extra inputs at test time.
method: Uses a hierarchical multi-teacher distillation framework to aggregate supervision from diverse proxy sources.
Treats proxies as mediators that inject complementary knowledge from viewpoints, modalities, and foundation models into egocentric learning.
Trains an egocentric-only student model that can be deployed from wearable video alone while inheriting broader representation power.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path to stronger egocentric video models without changing deployment constraints. It can improve downstream tasks like action recognition, retrieval, and anticipation by leveraging richer training signals than egocentric data alone.

paper_title: UNIEGO: Proxies as Mediators for Unified Egocentric Video Representation Learning
paper_authors: Wenhao Chi, Arkaprava Sinha, Dominick Reilly, Hieu Le, Srijan Das
